```{r a5-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", fig.width=6.5,
  fig.height=5.8, dpi=120, out.width="100%")
library(postrank)
fmt <- function(x, digits=4) formatC(x, digits=digits, format="f")
```

The posterior representation determines the uncertainty retained by an
analysis and the calculations available from it. postrank accepts joint
draws, criterion-specific draws, supported conditional distributions and
previously calculated comparison probabilities. Model fitting precedes this
input stage, and dependence omitted from an export cannot be recovered by
the package.

We construct a one-criterion input, extend the same example to two criteria
and obtain an alternative input from analytic probabilities. The examples
use a specified synthetic law with explicit source assumptions. Rendering
performs small draw-generation and aggregation calculations without an
optimizer. In an observed-data application, the synthetic generator is
replaced by output from the fitted model, with declarations describing that
model and its sampling history.

## Targets and posterior states {#decide-what-one-row-of-your-export-means}

Entity IDs identify the same sites, schools, firms or other units throughout
an analysis. Character labels preserve identifiers with leading zeros.
Criterion IDs identify the targets, including their units, time reference
and direction. On the oriented scale, larger values receive higher reporting
priority, with grade 1 denoting the highest-priority group.

Joint draws have array dimensions draw × entity × criterion. Each draw is
a joint state of all entities and criteria; its index cannot be interpreted
as an entity, parameter or arbitrary row from another fit. For a single
criterion, the final singleton dimension must be retained: the
\(S\times n\times1\) array records a criterion axis that R would otherwise
drop.

| What the producer supplies | Public entry point | Information to preserve |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Joint target draws | `postrank_draws()` | Entity/criterion axes, within-state pairing, sampling regime |
| Separate criterion matrices | `postrank_draws(..., metadata=)` | Joint entity vectors within each criterion and each block's own history |
| A conditional Gaussian law | `postrank_gaussian_coefficients()` | Means, covariance axes, conditional independence and source records |
| Shared-state Gaussian mixture | `postrank_mixture_coefficients()` | Common hyperstates, weights and conditional moments |
| An explicitly specified finite law | `as_postrank_draws()` | Complete states and exact declared masses |
| Comparison probabilities | `postrank_probabilities()` | Event direction, source assumptions, equality policy and numerical corrections |

The last four representations require the specified probability law or
comparison probabilities to be part of the intended analysis. A few retained
summaries alone do not identify the corresponding distribution of draws.

## A complete one-criterion draw example

`pr_tutorial$law` specifies normal distributions for fictional sites A
through F, with fixed means and variances. Sites are independent, and the
scores have illustrative standardized units without empirical calibration.
The resulting small array is generated from this specified law, without
observations or estimated hyperparameters.

```{r a5-generate-one}
library(postrank)
law <- pr_tutorial$law
ids <- rownames(law$means)
S <- 512L
sd_A <- sqrt(law$covariance["score_A", "score_A", ])
set.seed(725)
values <- array(NA_real_, c(S, length(ids), 1L),
  dimnames = list(draw = NULL, entity = ids, criterion = "score_A"))
for (i in seq_along(ids)) {
  values[, i, 1] <- rnorm(S, law$means[i, "score_A"], sd_A[i])
}
dim(values)
```

The generator produces `r S` independent states of `r length(ids)` sites.
For fitted posterior output, target draws should be exported at their
retained precision. Independent simulation from marginal means and standard
deviations is justified only when independence and normality are assumptions
of the intended model.

The array constructor requires eight scientific declarations. The following
metadata describe this generator; an empirical analysis requires declarations
appropriate to its model and output.

```{r a5-declarations}
declarations <- postrank_declarations(
  targets = data.frame(
    criterion_id = "score_A",
    estimand = "Site-level latent score A in the specified Gaussian law",
    entity_population = "Six fictional sites A through F",
    time_reference = "Static tutorial scenario; no observed time period",
    units = law$units
  ),
  context = list(
    cohort_id = "pr-tutorial-six-sites", data_version = "1",
    data_conditioning = "No observations; all means and variances fixed by pr_tutorial$law",
    model_summary = "Independent site Gaussian scores with the supplied means and variances"
  ),
  provenance = list(
    producer = "A5 tutorial R generator", artifact_id = "a5-iid-score-A",
    construction_note = "512 independent states sampled with rnorm after set.seed(725)"
  ),
  origin = list(
    source_id = "pr-tutorial-fixed-law", fit_id = "hand-specified-law-no-fit",
    model_id = "independent-site-Gaussian", source_format = "R numeric array",
    source_artifact = "a5-your-posterior-results.Rmd using pr_tutorial$law"
  ),
  identification_note = "Each target is a directly specified coordinate of the fixed law; no latent-label ambiguity remains.",
  tie_justification = "Independent continuous normal site scores have positive variances, so distinct-site equality has probability zero.",
  joint_generation = "Each draw contains all six sites from one independent state of the specified score-A law.",
  sampling_provenance = "Base R rnorm generated IID states with seed 725; no warmup, discarding or thinning was performed."
)
draws <- postrank_draws(values, regime = "iid", declarations = declarations)
draws$entity_ids
draws$criterion_ids
```

`targets` specifies the quantities compared, and `context` the information
on which the posterior conditions. `provenance` identifies the exported
result, whereas `origin` identifies its producing source and model. The
remaining declarations describe identification, zero equality probability,
joint-state construction and sampling. In particular, shared effects in a
hierarchical model must remain shared within draws. Independently shuffling
entity draws would change the comparison distribution while preserving
marginal histograms.

For a raw criterion on which smaller values receive higher priority,
`orientation = c(rate = "lower")` in the high-level array constructor negates
the criterion and records the transformation. The supplied values should
therefore remain on the raw rate scale to avoid applying the sign change
twice. The [school accountability example](a2-cde-accountability.html)
describes the resulting negative-rate target.

### Pairwise comparison probabilities {#inspect-the-comparisons-before-choosing-grades}

```{r a5-aggregate-one}
pairwise <- postrank_pairwise(draws)
round(pairwise$e[, , "score_A"], 3)
```

Entry \(e_{ij}\) estimates \(\Pr(\theta_i\leq\theta_j)\): the expected
error if entity `i` is placed above entity `j`. The diagonal is `NA` because
an entity is not compared with itself. A finite off-diagonal zero means that
the event did not occur in these retained draws; it does not prove a zero
probability in the underlying continuous law.

The stored array retains the singleton criterion axis. Subsetting by
`larger_array[, , "score_A", drop = FALSE]` preserves it. Continuous draws
should retain their numerical precision: rounding can introduce observed
ties, which this tie-free route rejects, while jitter changes the declared
posterior. Models with genuine equality mass use the separate input domain
specified in `?as_postrank_tie_draws`.

## Joint criteria and separate criterion fits

We extend the simulation to score B while retaining every score-A draw.
The tutorial law specifies independence of the scores within sites; this
assumption is particular to the example.

```{r a5-two-criteria}
two_values <- array(NA_real_, c(S, length(ids), 2L),
  dimnames = list(draw = NULL, entity = ids, criterion = colnames(law$means)))
two_values[, , "score_A"] <- values[, , "score_A"]
for (i in seq_along(ids)) {
  two_values[, i, "score_B"] <- rnorm(S, law$means[i, "score_B"],
    sqrt(law$covariance["score_B", "score_B", i]))
}
two_declarations <- unclass(declarations)
two_declarations$targets <- data.frame(
  criterion_id = colnames(law$means),
  estimand = c("Site-level latent score A", "Site-level latent score B"),
  entity_population = "Six fictional sites A through F",
  time_reference = "Static tutorial scenario; no observed time period",
  units = law$units
)
two_declarations$provenance$artifact_id <- "a5-iid-score-A-and-B"
two_declarations$joint_generation <- paste(
  "Each draw contains all sites and both criteria from one state;",
  "sites and criteria are mutually independent under the specified tutorial law."
)
two_draws <- postrank_draws(two_values, regime = "iid",
  declarations = do.call(postrank_declarations, two_declarations))
two_pairwise <- postrank_pairwise(two_draws)
identical(pairwise$e[, , "score_A"], two_pairwise$e[, , "score_A"])
```

Row indices from separate criterion fits generally do not identify common
posterior states. Such output is represented by a named list of
\(S_k\times n\) matrices, each row containing a complete entity vector.
`postrank_draws(matrices, metadata = criterion_metadata)` accepts these
matrices with canonical criterion-wise metadata. Each block records its
origin, sampling history, original draw coordinates and variable map, while
the matrix supplies the values. Retained draw counts may differ between
criteria. The required structure is documented in `?postrank_draws`.

This representation supports additive criterion-wise expected loss without
a cross-criterion joint state. Composite ordering probabilities and
simultaneous correctness probabilities remain unidentified. Dependence
between entities within each criterion must still be retained: aligning
unrelated marginal samples is justified only when the producing model
supports that construction.

MCMC output requires its sampling history. A regular array layout specifies
`regime = "mcmc"`, the number of `chains`, removed `warmup_per_chain` and
retained-iteration spacing `thin`, with `thin = 1L` denoting no thinning.
Rows are stored chain by chain. A large draw count does not justify
reclassifying MCMC output as IID. For `posterior` draws objects or irregular
layouts, `?as_postrank_posterior` describes explicit variable mappings and
source coordinates. The adapter verifies mappings and declared history;
convergence requires separate assessment.

## Analytic probabilities under a Gaussian law {#a-gaussian-law-can-supply-probabilities-directly}

When the intended conditional law is Gaussian, directional probabilities
can be calculated without simulation. Here the analytic calculation uses
the same tutorial parameters and their recorded source information.

```{r a5-analytic}
analytic <- postrank_gaussian_coefficients(
  means = law$means[, "score_A", drop = FALSE],
  covariance = law$covariance["score_A", "score_A", , drop = FALSE],
  conditional_independence = "entities_given_shared_h",
  provenance = pr_tutorial$one$provenance
)
selected_pairs <- rbind(c(1L, 2L), c(3L, 4L), c(5L, 6L))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  row = ids[selected_pairs[, 1]], column = ids[selected_pairs[, 2]],
  draw_estimate = pairwise$e[, , 1][selected_pairs],
  analytic = analytic$e[, , 1][selected_pairs]
), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

The two columns concern the same target law but use different numerical
calculations. The draw estimate varies with the retained simulation, whereas
the analytic value follows from the normal distribution of the difference
between conditionally independent site scores. Neither calculation refits
the model. The Gaussian constructor requires named entity and criterion
axes, positive-definite covariance matrices, an explicit
conditional-independence declaration, and source records tied to the
producer inputs. A different producer requires its own records and hashes.

In a hierarchical model, averaging conditional probabilities over common
hyperstates can preserve dependence induced by shared hyperparameters.
`?postrank_mixture_coefficients` describes the constructor, including fixed
mixture weights and hyperparameter-MCMC coordinates. A single Gaussian with
matched moments generally defines a different law.

An exact finite posterior specifies complete states, integer mass
numerators and a common denominator. It enters through `as_postrank_draws()`
and can retain rational comparison coefficients with the optional `gmp`
package. These masses define the probability law; a finite Monte Carlo
sample remains an approximation even though its storage is finite. The
finite-state and criterion-block layouts are supplied in
`system.file("schema", "draws-schema.json", package = "postrank")`;
`?as_postrank_draws` and `?postrank_pairwise` document construction and
aggregation.

## Externally calculated comparison probabilities {#import-probabilities-without-inventing-a-posterior-sample}

An external integration routine may provide directional probabilities
directly. `postrank_probabilities()` accepts a named square matrix for one
criterion or an entity-by-entity-by-criterion array, together with an explicit
event definition. The following input uses the analytic probabilities above
and means and intervals from the same normal law.

```{r a5-probability-input}
means <- law$means[, "score_A", drop = FALSE]
level <- .9
half_width <- qnorm((1 + level) / 2) * sd_A
probability_input <- postrank_probabilities(
  analytic$e[, , "score_A"], criterion = "score_A",
  event = "directional_error", zero_ties = TRUE, margin = 0,
  source = list(
    kind = "analytic_reference",
    description = "Normal-CDF comparisons for independent site scores in pr_tutorial$law",
    conditioning = law$conditioning
  ),
  targets = c(score_A = "Illustrative standardized site score A; larger is higher priority"),
  summaries = list(
    means = means, same_targets = TRUE,
    description = "Means and central equal-tail intervals from the same fixed normal site laws",
    lower = sweep(means, 1, half_width, "-"),
    upper = sweep(means, 1, half_width, "+"), level = level
  )
)
probability_input$correction$method
```

Both entity axes must have the same IDs in the same order. Diagonals are
`NA`, off-diagonals lie between zero and one, and reverse directions sum to
one within the validation tolerance. This route requires declared zero
equality probability and zero comparison margin. Range and complement
checks do not prove that an arbitrary collection of probabilities comes
from a coherent joint posterior or a suitable model.

```{r a5-probability-map, fig.cap="Directional-error probabilities from the specified one-criterion normal law. Grey diagonal cells are not comparisons; they are not zero-probability observations."}
postrank_plot_pairwise(probability_input, max_entities = NULL)
```

Small reverse-complement discrepancies can be corrected by explicitly
requesting `correction = "symmetric"` and declaring a `tolerance`. The
object retains the raw probabilities and maximum adjustment. This adjustment
measures the change to the supplied values, without bounding quadrature
error, Monte Carlo error or model uncertainty.

Supplied summaries must concern the same oriented targets and units as the
probabilities. The intervals here have level `r 100*level`%; other levels
are not identified by their endpoints. The probability input has no implied
draw count or Monte Carlo standard error, and structural validation does not provide
a numerical certificate. The [employer case](a3-krw-race-gender.html) uses
this representation with integrated continuous-cell probabilities in place
of a normal approximation.

## Structural validation and model assessment {#keep-validation-and-model-checking-separate}

The high-level array constructor groups the declarations and checks their
text for generic placeholders. The strict `postrank_draws_from_array()`
constructor accepts the same eight declarations separately. Canonical JSON,
criterion-wise metadata and the `posterior` bridge apply their respective
structural and declaration-presence checks; the high-level constructor's text check is not
implied by acceptance through these routes. Identification, independence
and convergence remain scientific assumptions or properties requiring
assessment beyond constructor validation.

```{r a5-strict-route}
strict_draws <- do.call(postrank_draws_from_array,
  c(list(values = values, regime = "iid"), unclass(declarations)))
identical(draws$joint_draws$tensor$values,
  strict_draws$joint_draws$tensor$values)
```

```{r a5-validation}
validation <- validate_postrank_draws(draws)
validation[c("valid", "source_values_checked", "jointness_verified",
             "convergence_verified")]
```

Structural validity complements the producer's model checks. An empirical
analysis also requires an identified target, correct sampling history,
explicit posterior conditioning and an export preserving the intended joint
states. For empirical-Bayes inputs, estimated prior quantities treated as
fixed must be specified: the resulting conditional uncertainty excludes
uncertainty in those estimates unless it has been propagated separately.

The following call specifies the reporting loss and constraints once the
input is constructed. It is displayed without executing a solver. For this
weighted at-most-G example, `analytic` or `probability_input` may replace
`draws`, subject to the distinct numerical and diagnostic capabilities of
each representation.

```{r a5-optional-solve, eval=FALSE}
result <- postrank(draws, weights = c(score_A = 1), tau = .25,
  G_max = 3L, backend = "highs", level = .9,
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 30), fragility = FALSE)
```

its grades and withheld comparisons.

how to retain the resulting tables and their numerical status.
